quiz.title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions: Principal Values Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the principal values and ranges of sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹ and their friends, exactly as in NCERT Exercise 2.1. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Principal values of inverse trigonometric functions

questions.q: What is the principal value of sin⁻¹(1/2)?
questions.explanation: sin⁻¹ returns an angle in [−π/2, π/2]. Since sin(π/6) = 1/2 and π/6 lies in that range, the principal value is π/6.

questions.q: What is the principal value of cos⁻¹(−1/2)?
questions.explanation: cos⁻¹ returns an angle in [0, π], where cosine is negative in the second quadrant. cos(2π/3) = −1/2, so the principal value is 2π/3.

questions.q: What is the principal value of tan⁻¹(−1)?
questions.explanation: tan⁻¹ returns an angle in (−π/2, π/2). tan(−π/4) = −1 and −π/4 lies in that open interval, so the value is −π/4.

questions.q: What is the range (set of principal values) of cos⁻¹ x?
questions.explanation: The principal value branch of cos⁻¹ is the closed interval [0, π]. The endpoints are included because cos⁻¹(1) = 0 and cos⁻¹(−1) = π.

questions.q: What is the value of sin⁻¹(sin 2π/3)?
questions.explanation: 2π/3 is outside [−π/2, π/2], so you cannot cancel directly. sin(2π/3) = √3/2, and the angle in the principal range with that sine is π/3.

questions.q: What is the principal value of sec⁻¹(2)?
questions.explanation: sec⁻¹ returns an angle in [0, π] excluding π/2. sec(π/3) = 1/cos(π/3) = 1/(1/2) = 2, so the principal value is π/3.

questions.q: What is the principal value of tan⁻¹(√3)?
questions.explanation: tan(π/3) = √3 and π/3 lies in (−π/2, π/2), the principal branch of tan⁻¹. So the value is π/3.

questions.q: What is the principal value of cot⁻¹(−1)?
questions.explanation: cot⁻¹ returns an angle in (0, π). cot(3π/4) = −1 and 3π/4 lies in that interval, so the principal value is 3π/4, not −π/4.

faq.q: What does Exercise 2.1 of Class 12 Inverse Trigonometric Functions cover?
faq.a: It asks only for the principal values of inverse trigonometric functions — sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹, cosec⁻¹, sec⁻¹ and cot⁻¹ of standard numbers. There is no simplification or proof here; the whole exercise is about picking the correct angle from each function's principal branch.

faq.q: What is a principal value and why does each function need one?
faq.a: Trigonometric functions repeat, so equations like sin x = 1/2 have infinitely many solutions. To make the inverse a genuine function, we restrict its output to one fixed interval. The single answer from that interval is called the principal value.

faq.q: What are the principal value ranges I must memorise?
faq.a: sin⁻¹ and cosec⁻¹ use [−π/2, π/2]; cos⁻¹ and cot⁻¹ use [0, π] (open for cot⁻¹); tan⁻¹ uses (−π/2, π/2); sec⁻¹ uses [0, π] excluding π/2. Getting these ranges right is what the exercise tests.

faq.q: Why is cos⁻¹(−1/2) equal to 2π/3 and not −π/3?
faq.a: Because cos⁻¹ must return a value in [0, π], which has no negative angles. Cosine is negative in the second quadrant, so the correct principal value is 2π/3. The same care with the range decides every negative-argument question in this exercise.
